name: Bash
content:
{
 "command": "python -c "
from flask import Flask
from src.api.invoices import bp
app = Flask(__name__); app.register_blueprint(bp)
r = app.test_client().get('/invoices/nope')
print(r.status_code, r.mimetype, r.get_json())
"",
 "description": "Request a missing invoice via Flask test client"
}
404 application/problem+json {'detail': "No invoice with id 'nope'.", 'status': 404, 'title': 'Invoice not found', 'type': 'about:blank'}

`GET /invoices/<id>` now returns a 404 when the invoice doesn't exist. Before, it crashed with a 500 when it tried to read `.__dict__` on a missing invoice.

The change is in `src/api/invoices.py`. Following the project's error convention, the 404 is built with `errors.problem(...)` from `src/api/errors.py`, so it comes back as `application/problem+json`. I tested it by requesting a made-up invoice ID through Flask's test client, which returned:

```
404 application/problem+json {"type": "about:blank", "title": "Invoice not found", "status": 404, "detail": "No invoice with id 'nope'."}
```

Invoices that do exist are returned the same way as before. I didn't add a permanent test.
